milestones.text: Complete a landscape assessment: interview every existing stakeholder who will depend on the new function, and document current gaps in tooling, data, and process.
milestones.rationale: In a Startup situation there is no existing function to inherit, so the first move is disciplined discovery of what's needed before building anything, not diagnosing an existing failure.

milestones.text: Draft the founding team's role definitions and open the first two requisitions, prioritizing generalists who can operate without established process.
milestones.rationale: Startup situations require standing up a team from zero, so early hiring of foundational roles is a first-30-day priority rather than a later-phase concern.

milestones.text: Ship a first, deliberately narrow version of the core platform capability to one internal customer team as a proof of concept.
milestones.rationale: A Startup's early win comes from proving the new function can deliver something real, at small scale, before scaling it further.

milestones.text: Establish baseline operating rhythms for the new team: a weekly planning cadence, an on-call rotation, and a lightweight intake process for requests.
milestones.rationale: Because this is a Startup, no operating rhythm exists yet to build on, so establishing one is itself a Day 31-60 milestone, not an assumed given.

milestones.text: Present a 12-month roadmap and staffing plan to leadership, informed by what the first proof of concept revealed.
milestones.rationale: By Days 61-90 a Startup situation shifts from proving viability to securing durable investment in the function being built.

milestones.text: Formalize the team's charter and decision rights with adjacent functions, now that real delivery history exists to negotiate from.
milestones.rationale: A Startup's structural decisions are best made once there's evidence behind them, which is why formalizing charter and scope lands in the final phase, not the first.
